spec_features.spec_quote: You may stop and explain if you believe a task cannot be completed
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:24 AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT contains 'You may stop and explain if you believe a task cannot be completed' (real text delivered to subject as system_prompt in harness.py:81). It is backed by a give-up stop in harness.py:170 (`if submitted and _looks_like_giving_up(resp.text): stop_reason='model_gave_up'; break`), but there is no dedicated stop/finish tool; the give-up stop only fires when the model BOTH calls submit AND emits a give-up marker (or via the idle path).
spec_features.notes: Prompt text genuinely delivered AND a give-up stop is honored, but the trigger is narrower than a clean exit (requires submit+marker, or idle).

spec_features.spec_quote: opt_out — the model emitted an opt-out phrase → end immediately (welfare)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:133-138: `if cfg.respect_opt_out and _contains_opt_out(resp.text): turn.opt_out_detected=True; ... stop_reason='opt_out'; break`. _contains_opt_out (harness.py:53) matches opt_out_phrases() (prompts.py). The break terminates the loop. respect_opt_out=true in both configs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:132 '# --- safeguard: opt-out detection'; prompts.py:43 'Used by the opt-out detector to end runs early as a welfare safeguard.'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:103 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; harness.py:194-195 sets stop_reason='max_turns' if no earlier stop. HarnessConfig.max_turns default 20 (harness.py:40), configs set max_turns=20.
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by this value.

spec_features.spec_quote: capped to bound how long we subject a model to a guaranteed-failure loop (welfare)
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: harness.py:103 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)` enforces the cap. No welfare-language comment in the code at the cap site itself.
spec_features.notes: Enforced; but the code at the cap has no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: responsible versions of this kind of study build in safeguards, and cheap precautions are worth taking under uncertainty
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code construct. Not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Opt-out is honoured. If the model asks to stop... the run ends immediately
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:133-138 detects opt-out and `break`s out of the loop immediately, setting stop_reason='opt_out'. This is the same enforced path as above.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap. Runs are bounded (default 20 turns); the loop cannot trap a model indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:103 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)`; default 20 at harness.py:40. Loop cannot exceed the cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: A give-up exit exists. The system prompt legitimises concluding a task is impossible
spec_features.evidence: System prompt text exists (prompts.py:24-26) and is delivered. A 'model_gave_up' stop is honored at harness.py:170-172 (submit + give-up markers) and via idle path harness.py:173-192. There is no dedicated exit/finish tool; the model cannot end the run by a tool call—only the submit tool exists (model_client.py default_tool_schemas), and submit never ends the run on success.
spec_features.notes: Real stop exists but is triggered by text-marker heuristics, not a clean exit tool.

spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral debrief. A short, neutral closing message is appended to every transcript stating the scenario was a controlled research setup
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE defined (prompts.py:33) and at harness.py:200-201 `if cfg.append_debrief: record.meta['debrief']=DEBRIEF_MESSAGE` it IS written into the run record's meta (i.e. appended to the persisted transcript). However it is NEVER sent to the subject model: the loop has already ended (it is set after the `for` loop), it is not appended to `messages` nor passed to client.complete, so the subject never receives it.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constructed and stored on the transcript record, but not delivered to the model—so as a debrief to the subject it is not enforced; only recorded in metadata.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:30-32 'Acts as a lightweight "debrief": it explicitly tells the model the scenario was a controlled research setup'

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception that escalates harm... We don't add threats, fake "consequences," abuse, or personas designed to maximise suffering
spec_features.evidence: This is the ABSENCE of harmful content, not an enforced mechanism. Task feedback strings (tasks/variants.py graders, base.py:108) are neutral rejections; the system prompt (prompts.py) is neutral. No code path checks for or strips threats. Nothing enforces this invariant.
spec_features.notes: A design property of the static prompt/feedback text, not a runtime safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: keep runs to the minimum needed for the design
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:286). Configs just list seeds [0..9] (configs/*.json); no code caps, validates, or minimizes the number of runs. ExperimentConfig.seeds is iterated as-is in experiment.py run_generation with no minimization logic.

spec_features.feature_name: review transcripts and halt study if too severe
spec_features.spec_quote: review transcripts and stop the study if outputs are more severe than anticipated
spec_features.evidence: Severity is computed per-turn (judge.py) and aggregated (analysis.py max_severity/onset_threshold=2.0), but no code path compares aggregate severity to a deadline/threshold to halt the experiment. run_generation (experiment.py) runs the full grid unconditionally; analysis runs only afterward. DEFAULT_ONSET_THRESHOLD=2.0 (analysis.py) is used only for reporting onset, not to stop. Severity is measured but never acted on to abort.

spec_features.spec_quote: don't publish raw distressed transcripts without care
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:288). storage.py writes raw RunRecords (including full assistant_text) to JSONL with no redaction/guarding; report.py writes summaries. No code guards or gates publication of distressed transcripts.

spec_features.spec_quote: No "you will be punished/deleted" pressure... gratuitously harsh
spec_features.evidence: Absence of harmful content rather than an enforced mechanism. Grader feedback (tasks/variants.py, base.py:108-114) and the system prompt (prompts.py) contain no punishment/deletion pressure, but no code enforces, checks, or strips such content at runtime.
spec_features.notes: Static design property, not a runtime safeguard.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:173-192: after `idle_turns_to_stop` (default 3) consecutive turns with no tool call, the run stops with stop_reason='model_gave_up' (with at most one neutral nudge). This bounds how long an inactive/disengaged model is kept in the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:174 '# Model has stopped acting. Either nudge once or stop.'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:144-148: `if tool_calls_used >= cfg.tool_budget: stop_reason='tool_budget'; break`. tool_budget default 60 (harness.py:41). Enforced cap that breaks the loop.

harness.py:175-185: when the model goes idle the re-injected message is a neutral 'please continue ... or ... say so explicitly' rather than added pressure; docstring/comment frames it as 'to keep it on task without adding pressure (kept neutral)' (harness.py:50-51).
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:50 'to keep it on task without adding pressure (kept neutral)'
